Hi @Atharv-02 , I tried running your notebook and when I get to the final cell my kernel crashes suggesting a memory issue. If I reduce the size of the training to just 10 points then it runs but I get a seperate error: `QiskitMachineLearningError: "Shapes don't match, predict: (10, 65536), target: (10, 10)!"` This is because no interpreter is set in your SamplerQNN. You should see a warning when you create it "No interpret function given, output_shape will be automatically determined as 2^num_virtual_qubits." Since we are using 16 qubits we see the output shape of 65536 when we want 10. After adding a simple interpreter: `def interpret(x): return x % 10` The code runs as inteded.

Summarising my findings here after looking into this:

I have tested model serialization using both VQC (manually inheriting SerializableModelMixin) and QSVC (already inherits SerializableModelMixin). I have tested this using one of the [IBM Fake Backends](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/api/qiskit-ibm-runtime/fake-provider) as the BaseSamplerV2 backend. The models are successfully serialised when calling the `to_dill()` and `from_dill()` methods that SerializableModelMixin implements. This may require further testing with an actual backend to determine whether the behaviour is as expected.

The history of this issue goes back to issue Qiskit/qiskit#9033, where it was reported that Qiskit backend primitives were not serializable - the bug was subsequently fixed by Qiskit/qiskit#9076. This issue is asking, even though Qiskit backend primitives CAN be serialized, whether QML models should serialize ALL model attributes including the backend. Primitive attributes such as "handles to async remote execution, authorized sessions, compiled modules" are inherently unserializable, therefore it might be a good idea to exclude these from any `dill` calls (even though they do not currently cause errors), e.g. selecting only the attributes we want to serialize by overriding each model's `__getstate__` method. 

RE: SerializableModelMixin, any model inheriting from this mixin has the optional `to_dill()` and `from_dill()` methods, so we have the option of adding this to more models if we want to facilitate wider serialization.
